outcomes: Each package of a Turborepo repository is a Putnami project, with an edge to each workspace package it depends on
In delegate mode, putnami lint, test and build run turbo run on each affected package, and Turborepo's cache, local and remote, decides what reruns
In import mode, a TypeScript package's task whose script already runs what @putnami/typescript runs moves to Putnami's runner and cache, and every other task keeps running through Turborepo
In delegate mode, the packages options["@putnami/turbo"].import selects are imported as import mode imports them, so a team moves one package at a time
nonGoals: Caching a Turborepo result in Putnami's cache, or putting Putnami's cache over Turborepo's
Mapping a turbo.json task other than build, test and lint: it keeps running through Turborepo
Installing or switching a Turborepo version: the repository's own turbo, in node_modules/.bin at the workspace root after its install, or a turbo on PATH runs

Rewriting turbo.json, or a package.json beyond the exports an import adds (D-066), or changing the tool that checks a task: a prettier task or an eslint task with arguments stays on Turborepo, and a build that runs tsc moves only with that tsc

text: At a root that holds turbo.json, the probe answers each member of the npm, pnpm or yarn workspace among the candidate directories: its package name as source name, the members it depends on as edges, the extension @putnami/turbo and the tag turbo, unless the package's putnami.json names other extensions.
The root and any other candidate are not answered.

The sync reads options["@putnami/turbo"].mode, import by default, and writes in each member's putnami.json @putnami/turbo, its edges as project IDs, and in disable.jobs each of build, test and lint it has no script or turbo.json task for.
In import mode a TypeScript package also names @putnami/typescript when a task moves to it, one whose script runs bun build, bun test, vitest, jest or biome;
the other extension's job of each task is disabled.
It retracts a former member and rewrites only a changed file.

In import mode, a TypeScript package whose lint script runs eslint or eslint . alone, plainly or through npx, bunx, pnpm exec or yarn, runs as @putnami/typescript:lint, which lints it with ESLint because its lint script runs eslint.
A lint script with other ESLint arguments, or that chains another command such as prettier, keeps running through Turborepo and is listed.

In delegate mode, the sync reads options["@putnami/turbo"].import, or the import parameter in its place: package paths and globs matched against each package's directory, a leading / ignored, * ? [...] within one segment.
Each selected package is written as import mode writes it, the others stay delegated, and an entry that selects none is listed as turbo.import_unmatched.
Import mode reads no list. validate fails with turbo.sync_stale when a putnami.json does not match the list.

requirements.text: With the dry-run parameter, and the mode parameter in place of the configured mode, the sync prints the unified diff of each putnami.json it would change, and writes nothing.

text: The sync lists, with the reason, each turbo.json task other than build, test and lint, and in import mode each task of a TypeScript package whose script runs something other than what @putnami/typescript runs: both keep running through Turborepo.
It also lists each package whose delegated test task names no JUnit report, whose result is then the exit code alone.

requirements.text: putnami validate compares each member's putnami.json with what the sync would write, writes nothing, and fails with turbo.sync_stale when a sync would change one, such as after a package manifest gains or loses a workspace dependency.

text: Each lint, test and build task of a @putnami/turbo package runs turbo run <task> --filter=<package name> at the workspace root, after turbo --version, both with the root node_modules/.bin first on PATH.
With no turbo there or on PATH, the sync warns with stacks.toolchain_missing.
Turborepo's dependsOn runs the upstream tasks and its cache answers them.
Each task depends only on its package's graph step, which runs nothing; Putnami's cache is off, and the result records delegatedTo turbo.
The test task reads the JUnit and coverage reports that options["@putnami/turbo"].tasks.test.reports of the package's putnami.json names into the test and coverage summary;
a failed case fails the task with stacks.test_failed.
Without them, the task's result is the exit code alone.

requirements.text: The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the turbo:lint, turbo:test and turbo:build selectors, each command runs the graph step, which depends on the graph step upstream, then its task, which depends on its own graph step alone, and every task sets cache.enabled to false.

text: In import mode, an imported TypeScript package whose package.json start script runs node gets options["@putnami/typescript"].runtime node in its putnami.json.
The sync never changes a runtime the package already declares.

In import mode, a TypeScript package's build task whose package.json script runs tsc alone, as @putnami/typescript's compiler choice reads it, moves to @putnami/typescript, which compiles it with that tsc.
A build script that runs tsc with another argument or a shell operator keeps running through Turborepo and is listed with its reason.

In import mode, an imported TypeScript project gets the conventions of D-066: exports {".": "./src/index.ts"} after the top-level main or types of a package.json that declares no exports, names a file outside src/, holds src/index.ts and is private, when its build moves to the Bun build;
a tsconfig.json extending the root's when it holds no tsconfig*.json.
The sync lists each write and each manifest it does not edit, and a dry sync shows each diff.
In import mode, a script that moves to @putnami/typescript does what it did: a test script moves with options["@putnami/typescript:test"].types false, since the script type-checked nothing.
A bun build script moves only when Putnami's Bun build writes the entries the package.json names: none outside src/, or entries D-066 rewrites; otherwise it stays on Turborepo and the sync says why.
When a lint moves, the sync says that putnami lint --impacted lints the projects a change touches, not their dependents.
In import mode, a lint script with no write flag moves with options["@putnami/typescript:lint"].fix false: the lint checks and rewrites no file.
When a Biome lint moves and the repository root holds no biome.json or biome.jsonc, the sync writes a root biome.json that sets nothing, so the lint keeps Biome's defaults, and lists it.
In import mode, a package names @putnami/typescript only when one of its tasks moves to it; a package none of whose tasks moves runs on Turborepo alone.
The sync declares a language extension in putnami.workspace.json only when a package names it: an import that moves no task leaves the workspace config, every manifest and the lockfile as they were.
